The source fidels are unchanged. Breath/spirit remains a lexical range, not a new doctrine; the opening and ending still follow the selected Geʽez, including singular “with it,” rather than replacing the whole verse with Greek.

translation.text: Before this, you have seen the destruction of your beloved children,[a] and you will have no benefit from them;[b] instead, they will fall before you by the sword.

footnotes.text: The selected Geʽez opening is cast as “you have seen”; that form is retained rather than silently changed to the different Greek purposive “that you may see.” It is not a new chronological assertion.

The selected daggered possessor-word construction is not certified as meaning “benefit.” This clause instead follows the printed Greek οὐκ ἔσται ὑμῖν ὄνησις αὐτῶν, “you will have no benefit from them,” on Charles printed37/PDF75. The apparatus discusses benefit/remnant possibilities; no remnant-word is inserted into Geʽez, and no manuscript uniformity is claimed. All other clauses retain the selected Ethiopic basis.
